newsitem.title: USA: Ohio says suspected molester back home in Tanzania.
newsitem.headline: Ohio says suspected molester back home in Tanzania.

text.p: Ohio authorities said on Friday they were unlikely to pursue a foreign exchange student believed to have returned to her native Tanzania after being suspected of sexually molesting girls at a Girl Scout camp.

Tim Oliver, chief prosecutor in neighbouring Warren County, said he had received information that the student, who was a counsellor at Camp Butterworth 20 miles (32 km) north of Cincinnati, flew back to the East African country on Wednesday.
"We have asked (the U.S. Immigration and Naturalisation Service) to confirm whether she has left this country and to detain her if she has not left," Oliver told Reuters.
"Frankly, we are very sceptical if we can bring her back to face any charges if she is now in Tanzania," he said.

The camp counsellor was put aboard a bus to New York City on Monday before she could be questioned by police about the incidents, which allegedly involved touching the buttocks and breasts of 10- and 11-year-old girls.

"We strongly believe that whatever happened has been blown way out of proportion," said Barbara Bonifas, executive director of the Great Rivers Girl Scout Council, which runs the camp. "Our camp staff members who were with this young woman at all times say they never saw anything out of the ordinary."
She reiterated that camp officials deeply regretted not notifying police immediately about the incidents.
"We have never had anything like this in the 60 years we have operated this camp and you can be sure if anything questionable ever arises again, we will notify the police right away," she said.
